body:
Properties of Matter: 1. When you pump air into a ball, the air takes up space and the ball gets a little heavier, so air has mass. 2. How easily heat or electricity moves through a material; the text says, "Does heat or electricity move through it easily? That property is called conductivity." 3. Any two: hardness, whether a magnet pulls on it, conductivity, solubility. 4. Physical: "In a physical change, like melting ice or dissolving salt, the material is still the same substance." 5. Any two: a new color, a gas, heat or light given off. 6. 265 grams; the total mass stays the same when matter changes, so 250 + 15 = 265.
Does Temperature Change How Fast Sugar Dissolves?: A strong hypothesis is testable and gives a reason (for example, warm water will dissolve sugar faster because its particles move faster). A fair test changes only the water temperature and keeps the cup, the amount of water, the amount of sugar and the stirring the same, with more than one trial. Data are recorded in °C and seconds; typical results show the warmest water dissolving the sugar fastest. The conclusion names the numbers (for example, 28 s at 45 °C against 95 s at 10 °C) and says whether the hypothesis was supported.
Matter Check: 1. Chemical change; evidence: it fizzed and bubbled (a gas formed, which puffed up the bag) and the bag felt cold (a temperature change). 2. 280 grams before and 280 grams after; mass is conserved: the matter changed into new substances, but none was lost or added. 3. 280 g = 0.28 kg, because 1 kg = 1,000 g and 280 ÷ 1,000 = 0.28. 4. Less than 280 grams: the gas escapes from the open bag into the air, so it is not weighed. The matter still exists; it is just not on the scale. 5. Sample A; any two of: a magnet pulls on it, electricity flows through it, it is shiny. 6. Add water and stir: Sample B dissolves and the sand does not. Pour the mixture through a filter (or a paper towel) to catch the sand, then let the water evaporate to get Sample B back.
Scoring tip: for question 4, "less" with the reason that gas escapes is Proficient on reasoning; adding that the mass of the matter itself did not change is Advanced.
title: Answer key: Matter and Its Properties
